messages:
marta: Quick Q — can we export audit logs as partitioned Parquet (for Snowflake) and what is the internal approval/permission flow for ad-hoc exports? Also: are PII columns redacted by default? cc @devon @jenna

devon: Short version: yes, parquet is supported by the export API. Endpoint is internal-only: POST /internal/audit/exports with payload {format: \"parquet\", partition_by: \"date\"}. Only roles with `audit_admin` or `security_ops` may create exports. Exports estimated >1M rows trigger a manual approval step. :gear:

sam: For customer-facing requests we route through support + prod SRE. Support creates a ticket, we validate least-privilege access, and SRE kicks off the export (or hands back with runbook instructions). If it's an internal ad-hoc, follow the security-approvals flow below.

jenna: Compliance note: PII (email, ip_address, user_id when mapped to PII) is redacted by default when the export call includes `redaction: \"auto\"`. If you explicitly pass `redaction: \"none\"` the request requires sign-off from Security + Legal (and an entry in the approval ticket).

marta: Can you paste a minimal example and where the files appear?

devon: Example (internal-only):
```
curl -X POST \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  https://api.redwood.local/internal/audit/exports \
  -d '{"format":"parquet","partition_by":"event_date","redaction":"auto","query":"event_time >= \"2026-12-01\""}'
```
Output location (default): s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/exports/<export-id>/part-*.parquet (Snappy compressed). Short policy notes: ad-hoc exports TTL = 90 days; automated retention exports for compliance are archived on glacier for 7 years via legal requests.

audit-bot: Export job queued: id=exp-20261201-43 by devon, estimated_rows=2.3M, state=AWAITING_APPROVAL.

sam: Approval process we use: create a ticket in #security-approvals and include export-id, dataset description, why you need raw rows vs. aggregated, and proposed TTL. Security on-call (daily rotation) will triage; if data sensitivity is high we escalate to Legal. Typical turnaround is a few hours during working hours.

jenna: Additional details: Parquet schema evolves; we publish Glue catalog entries to s3://redwood-audit-catalog/prod/ — recommend using the catalog under account role `analytics_read` rather than direct S3 listing. Also we strip raw IPs unless requester has explicit approved need.

marta: Perfect, thanks. I'll open the ticket and tag @devon + @jenna and include the customer justification. :thumbsup:
